title: Output
body:
`cout`, from `#include <iostream>`. The `<<` operator chains, so one statement can print
several things.

```c++
cout << "Total: " << total << endl;
```

`endl` is a newline **plus a flush**; `"\n"` is just the newline. Either is fine here.

Formatting numbers needs `#include <iomanip>`:

```c++
cout << fixed << setprecision(2) << price;   // 3.50 rather than 3.5
cout << setw(10) << name;                    // pad to 10 columns
```

`fixed` and `setprecision` stay set until changed; `setw` applies to the **next** item only,
which is why table code repeats it every column.

By default a [[Double]] prints six significant digits, which quietly hides the precision
problem rather than fixing it.

The other sense of "output" in this course is what a [[Function]] gives back. A function
returns at most one value, so a function with two results writes them through
[[Call by reference|reference parameters]] instead, which is what the [[IPO Diagram]]'s output
box turns into. [[Parameter]] says the same thing from the parameter side.

`cerr` is the error stream: unbuffered, and separate from `cout` so a [[Shell]] can redirect
one without the other.
